relevance_note: Narrative review of paediatric Behçet’s disease in which HA20 appears only at group level (e.g. “five families of different ethnicities with autosomal dominant, high-penetrance mutations in TNFAIP3 (Table 2)”, “a recent study involving 16 patients with A20 haploinsufficiency”); no individual with a stated TNFAIP3 variant is described in the available text.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown manually; no script transcription. (1) The Markdown contains no table content: Tables 1, 2 and 3 are cited in the text but absent from the conversion. Table 2 is described as listing the TNFAIP3 mutations of the five Zhou et al. families ("Zhou et al. [13] reported on five families ... mutations in TNFAIP3 (Table 2)") and Table 3 as comparing HA20 phenotypes; if the published Table 2 gives per-family variants, those previously published individuals would need extraction from the original article, which was not possible here. (2) One previously published patient is mentioned in a single sentence: "a patient treated for longstanding intestinal BD-like symptoms was later diagnosed with A20 haploinsufficiency [91]". No variant, sex, age or other detail is given, so no TNFAIP3 variant is stated for this person; I did not create an individual row and set reports_individuals_with_tnfaip3_variant to false. This is borderline: a reviewer may prefer one individual row (label 'a patient', source_reference_in_review '[91]', no variants row). (3) Other HA20 mentions are group-level only, without individual detail: Aeschlimann et al. 16 patients [41]; Papadopoulou et al. 11 paediatric monogenic mimics, A20 haploinsufficiency among the diagnoses, no count [33]; "whole-exome sequencing in familial BD patients was able to identify loss-of-function mutations in TNFAIP3 [89]". (4) n_patients_reported left null: the authors give no count of TNFAIP3 patients described in this document. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null because the review has no patients of its own. (5) first_author: the header lists authors as surname then given name ('Romano Micol', 'Brogan Paul A.') and the contributions give initials 'O.K.C.', so the surname was read as 'Kul Cinar'. No contradictions found in the paper.
